Abstract, plainly: piecewise interpretations (Visser) generalize interpretations between first-order theories by letting formulae be interpreted using disjoint unions of definable sets; this captures constructions like the projective completion of an affine plane and yields an equivalence notion, piecewise bi-interpretability.
